newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim Dae-jung wins presidential nomination.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim Dae-jung wins presidential nomination.

text.p: Veteran South Korean opposition leader Kim Dae-jung was elected by his party on Monday to be its candidate in presidential elections in December.

It will be Kim's fourth run for office. He won the nomination for the National Congress for New Politics against one other candidate. The results were announced on live television by a senior party official.
Kim, 74, won the nomination by a landslide at a national convention of his party in Seoul. He took 3,224 votes against 907 for his rival, Chung Dai-chul.
Party faithful packed into a sports stadium gave Kim a standing ovation after the results were announced.
"I swear to transfer power from the ruling party to the opposition party for the first time in 50 years," the opposition firebrand told cheering delegates.

The National Congress and the smaller United Liberal Democrats have been discussing putting up a single candidate against the ruling New Korea Party's nominee, who has yet to be selected. President Kim Young-sam, whose image has been tarnished by a high-profile bribes scandal, is due to step down when his single term expires in February.
